2027-03-17.title: Wednesday of the Fifth Week of Lent
readings: He has sent his angel and delivered his servants who trusted in him
To you glory and praise for evermore
If the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed
2027-03-17.alt: Lenten weekday of the fifth week. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted throughout Lent. From the Fifth Sunday of Lent crosses and images may be veiled until the Passion is celebrated (where the bishops' conference allows). Liturgical colour: violet. Commemoration of St Patrick, bishop (its collect may be used). In Ireland, and in some other places, St Patrick is kept as a solemnity or feast.
2027-03-17.verse: Then Jesus said to the Jews who had believed in him, “If you continue in my word, you are truly my disciples; and you will know the truth, and the truth will make you free.”
theo: King Nebuchadnezzar has set up a golden statue, and everyone must fall down before it when the music plays. Three young Jews, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, refuse. Brought before the furious king, they give an answer that has strengthened believers ever since: “If our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the furnace of blazing fire and out of your hand, O king, let him deliver us. But if not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods.” But if not: their faithfulness does not depend on being rescued. The furnace is heated seven times hotter and they are thrown in bound. Then the king leaps up in amazement: “I see four men unbound, walking in the middle of the fire, and they are not hurt; and the fourth has the appearance of a god.” The Fathers saw in the fourth figure a foreshadowing of the Son of God, who comes into our fire. Instead of the usual Psalm, the Church today sings part of the hymn of the three young men from the Greek text of Daniel: “Blessed are you, O Lord, God of our ancestors, and to be praised and highly exalted forever.”

In the Gospel Jesus speaks of another kind of freedom: “If you continue in my word, you are truly my disciples; and you will know the truth, and the truth will make you free.” His hearers protest that as children of Abraham they have never been slaves. Jesus answers: “everyone who commits sin is a slave to sin… So if the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed.” The debate in this chapter is sharp, and it reflects the painful arguments between the early Christians and the synagogue of John's day; it is never a licence for contempt of the Jewish people, from whom, as Jesus says elsewhere, salvation comes (John 4:22). Today the Church remembers St Patrick (about 385 to about 461). Captured as a boy in Britain and enslaved in Ireland, he learned to pray on the hillsides while tending sheep. He escaped, became a priest and a bishop, and went back freely to the land of his slavery to bring it the Gospel. In his Confession he writes (in substance) that he was like a stone lying deep in the mud until the Mighty One lifted him up. Patrick knew both kinds of slavery and both kinds of freedom. Like the three young men, he served God whether or not he was spared, and the truth made him free.

live: Name one idol in your life, money, approval, a habit, and refuse to bow to it today.
Read and pray over one chapter of the Gospel of Mark today, preparing for Palm Sunday.
2027-03-17.prayer: Lord God of our ancestors, blessed are you and highly exalted for ever. Give us the faith of the three young men, who served you whether or not they were rescued, and walk with us in every fire. Lord Jesus, make us free from the slavery of sin. Through the prayers of St Patrick, who returned in love to the land of his captivity, make us bold witnesses of the Gospel. Amen.
altar: The Son who makes us free gives himself at the altar. In the Eucharist he walks with us in the fire of daily life, as the fourth figure walked with the three young men.

quick: Three young men refused to worship the golden statue, even if God did not rescue them.
God was with them in the fire, and they came out unharmed.
Jesus frees us from slavery to sin; St Patrick, once a slave, became the apostle of Ireland.
2027-03-17.action: Say St Patrick's prayer today: Christ with me, Christ before me, Christ behind me.
2027-03-17.question: Would I stay faithful to God even if he did not give me what I am asking for?

family.explain: A king ordered everyone to bow down to a big golden statue. Three young men said: we will only worship God. They were thrown into a fire, but God was with them and they were not even burnt! Jesus also says: if I make you free, you will be really free.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who are punished for their faith, and for the people of Ireland on St Patrick's day.
family.ask: Ask: “What are the golden statues today that people bow to instead of God?”

illus: St Patrick tells in his Confession how, as a teenage slave herding sheep in Ireland, he prayed a hundred times a day and almost as many times at night, in snow and frost and rain. Years later, when he could have stayed safe at home in Britain, he dreamed he heard the Irish calling him: come and walk among us again. He went back to the people who had enslaved him, this time free, and brought them Christ.

pm.open: Blessed are you, O Lord, God of our ancestors. Walk with us in the fire and make us free. Amen.
share: But if not… we will not serve your gods (Daniel 3:18). Is my faith a bargain or a gift of myself?
I see four men unbound, walking in the middle of the fire (Daniel 3:92). Where have I felt God with me in a fire?
If the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed (John 8:36). From what slavery do I need to be freed?
pm.resp: To you glory and praise for evermore.
interc: For Christians who suffer for refusing to deny their faith.
For all who are trapped in addiction or slavery of any kind, that the Son may set them free.
For the Church in Ireland and for Irish missionaries in India and across the world, through the prayers of St Patrick.
For victims of human trafficking, that they may be rescued and healed.
For our group, that we may continue in the word of Jesus.
pm.close: Father, your Son makes us free indeed. Keep us faithful in every trial. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, three young men stand before a furious king. Bow to the golden statue, or burn. They answer: if our God is able to deliver us, let him deliver us. But if not, we will not serve your gods (Daniel 3:17–18). Their faith does not depend on a rescue. They will be faithful either way.

They are thrown into the furnace, and the king sees four men walking in the fire, unbound and unharmed, and the fourth looks like a son of the gods. God does not always keep us out of the fire. He comes into it with us.

Jesus speaks of freedom: if you continue in my word, you will know the truth, and the truth will make you free. Everyone who commits sin is a slave to sin. So if the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed (John 8:31–36). The worst slavery is not chains on the hands, but sin in the heart.

St Patrick knew both. Enslaved as a boy in Ireland, he found God while tending sheep in the cold. Freed, he chose to return as a bishop to the land of his slavery, to make its people free in Christ. Let us ask today for faith that does not bargain and for the freedom only the Son can give. Amen.
kids: Children, three young men would not bow down to a golden statue, because they loved God. They were thrown into a fire, but God was with them, and they came out without even the smell of smoke! St Patrick was a slave as a boy, but he became a bishop and taught Ireland about Jesus. Say today: Christ with me, Christ before me, Christ behind me!

intro: Theme: “If the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed.”
Faith that does not bargain, God in the fire, and the freedom of the Son; St Patrick.

sub: Faith that does not depend on rescue.
q: If our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the furnace of blazing fire and out of your hand, O king, let him deliver us. But if not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods and we will not worship the golden statue that you have set up.
But Peter and the apostles answered, “We must obey God rather than any human authority.
points.apply: Name one idol you bow to, and refuse it this week for the love of God.

points.h: The fourth man in the fire
sub: God with us in the furnace.
q: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overwhelm you; when you walk through fire you shall not be burned, and the flame shall not consume you.
And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
points.apply: In your present trial, pray each day: Lord, walk with me in this fire.

points.h: The truth will make you free
q: I shall walk at liberty, for I have sought your precepts.
So if the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed.
points.apply: Bring your heaviest chain to confession before Easter, and let the Son set you free.

concl: The three young men and St Patrick served God whether or not they were spared.
The Son of God walks with us in the fire and makes us free indeed.
2027-03-17.resolve: Pray St Patrick's Breastplate each morning of Holy Week.
